metadata.title: Dry Eye: Developing Drugs for Treatment Guidance for Industry
metadata.topic: Draft guideline · FDA human drugs and biologics
metadata.legal_basis: FDA Guidance Document (21 CFR 10.115). Guidance states FDA's current thinking and is not binding unless a statute or regulation requires it; the official text governs.

candidates.statement: In general, FDA’s guidance documents do not establish legally enforceable responsibilities. 21 Instead, guidances describe the Agency’s current thinking on a topic and should be viewed only 22 as recommendations, unless specific regulatory or statutory requirements are cited. The use of 23 the word should in Agency guidances means that something is suggested or recommended, but 24 not required. 25
candidates.context: This guidance is intended to provide recommendations to sponsors regarding eligibility criteria, 17 trial design considerations, and efficacy endpoints to enhance clinical trial data quality and to 18 foster greater efficiency in development programs for drugs for the treatment of dry eye. 2 II. CONSIDERATIONS FOR CLINICAL TRIALS 28

candidates.statement: Sponsors developing drugs for the treatment of dry eye should consider the following regarding 32 trial design: 33
candidates.context: • Both traditional environmental exposure trials and challenge-model trials (utilizing a 35 controlled chamber with regulated temperature, air flow, humidity, etc.) can be acceptable. 36

candidates.statement: Sponsors developing drugs for the treatment of dry eye should consider the following regarding 52 comparative clinical trials: 53
candidates.context: • Water is known to be an effective component of topically applied treatments for dry eyes. 55 Therefore, in general, comparative clinical trials should use the investigational drug’s 56 vehicle as a control agent. 57

candidates.context: Sponsors developing drugs for the treatment of dry eye should consider the following regarding 52 comparative clinical trials: 53 • Trials should demonstrate statistical and clinical superiority over a vehicle control or 59 another treatment regimen. 60

candidates.statement: • Trials should demonstrate statistical and clinical superiority over a vehicle control or 59 another treatment regimen. 60
candidates.context: • Water is known to be an effective component of topically applied treatments for dry eyes. 55 Therefore, in general, comparative clinical trials should use the investigational drug’s 56 vehicle as a control agent. 57 • Clinical trials for the treatment of dry eyes, even with known effective therapies, can fail 62 to demonstrate efficacy. In the absence of good assay validation (sensitivity) methods 63 (inclusion of both a positive and negative concurrent control), FDA does not recommend 64 equivalence or noninferiority trials. 65

candidates.statement: Sponsors developing drugs for the treatment of dry eye should consider the following regarding 91 efficacy: 92
candidates.context: D. Efficacy Considerations 89 • In general, safety and efficacy should be demonstrated in at least two adequate and 94 well-controlled, multicenter independent trials. 95

candidates.statement: • In general, safety and efficacy should be demonstrated in at least two adequate and 94 well-controlled, multicenter independent trials. 95
candidates.context: Sponsors developing drugs for the treatment of dry eye should consider the following regarding 91 efficacy: 92 • FDA recommends that the sponsor demonstrate one of the following: 97

candidates.statement: • Efficacy for a sign and efficacy for a symptom do not have to be demonstrated in the same 127 clinical trial, but each should be demonstrated in more than one clinical trial. 128
candidates.context: • A subjective symptom improvement can also be demonstrated by showing a statistically 122 significant difference between the percentage of patients achieving a complete resolution 123 of the symptom. FDA does not recommend the use of anything less than complete 124 resolution (complete clearing of a sign or symptom) for a responder analysis. 125 • The sponsor should discuss with FDA any scoring methods or scales used to measure 130 efficacy variables and should submit a copy of the scoring methods or scales with the 131 protocol. 132

candidates.statement: Sponsors developing drugs for the treatment of dry eye should consider the following regarding 139 safety: 140
candidates.context: E. Safety Considerations 137 • The clinical program should include enough patients to identify adverse drug events that 142 occur at a rate of 1 percent or greater. To accomplish this, FDA recommends that 143 approximately 400 or more patients using the investigational drug complete treatment with 144 a concentration of the investigational drug at least as high as proposed for marketing and 145 with a frequency at least as frequent as proposed for marketing. 146

candidates.statement: Sponsors developing drugs for the treatment of dry eye should consider the following regarding 160 clinical evaluations: 161
candidates.context: F. Clinical Evaluations 158 • At a minimum, FDA recommends that the following evaluations be performed in each eye 163 and reported separately for each eye (regardless of which eye or eyes are treated): 164

candidates.statement: − A slit lamp examination of the anterior segment that includes the cornea, conjunctiva, 170 anterior chamber, iris, lids, and lashes. At a minimum, examinations should be 171 performed at baseline, midway through the trial, the end of treatment, and 2 weeks 172 after treatment discontinuation. 173
candidates.context: − A patient comfort examination before and after drug administration at every visit. 168 − Endothelial cell count, systemic clinical and laboratory evaluations, and dilated fundus 175 examinations at baseline and at the end of trial or at month 3 (whichever is later) in at 176 least one trial. 177

candidates.statement: Dry eye rarely occurs in the pediatric population. Sponsors should consider pediatric assessment 181 waiver requests when submitting their required pediatric study plans under the Pediatric Research 182 Equity Act. 3
candidates.context: 3 See section 505B(e)(1) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FD&C Act); 21 U.S.C. 355c(e)(1); and section 505B(a)(1)(A) of the FD&C Act; 21 U.S.C. 355c(a)(1)(A).
